<a class="language-switch" href="../../pt/posts-pt/fornecedores-campanha-2026/" hreflang="pt-BR" lang="pt-BR" aria-label="Ir para a versão em português desta página"><span aria-hidden="true">PT ↗</span> Português</a>

By 18 October 2026, 14,867 candidates had declared **R\$ 4.64 billion in
contracted expenses** to Brazil's electoral court (TSE). The campaigns' largest
single supplier is **Meta** (Facebook Serviços Online do Brasil): **R\$ 289
million paid directly, 6.2% of all contracted spending**, by 6,131 candidates.
No printer, agency or production company comes close. The second company is
dLocal, an ad-payment intermediary, with R\$ 102 million.

::: {.callout-warning title="Contracted, self-reported and still partial"}
**Values are contracted expenses, not payments.** They include commitments that
may not have left the campaign account yet. The TSE publishes paid expenses in a
separate file, with smaller totals.

**Reporting is not finished.** The data mix partial reports, financial reports
and final accounts, and they change with each TSE update. Candidates who declared
nothing do not appear; second-round spending is included where applicable.

**These are the campaigns' own declarations.** The TSE has not yet ruled on these
accounts. Entry errors, duplicates and later corrections are possible.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="What counts as “Meta, direct”"}
We sum only payments to the CNPJs of Facebook Serviços Online do Brasil
(root 13.347.016) and Meta Platforms. **Excluded** are ads that reach Meta by
other routes:

- **Payment intermediaries** (dLocal and Ebanx, R\$ 115 million). Part of this pays
  for Meta ads, but descriptions name Facebook, Instagram or Meta for only R\$ 35
  million. The panels show these intermediaries separately.
- **Agencies** buying media for the campaign. For the TSE, the supplier is the
  agency, not the platform.

The direct amount is therefore a lower bound on what Meta received.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Estimate: between R\$ 289 and R\$ 404 million for Meta"}
Campaigns contracted **R\$ 415 million in content boosting** (a TSE expense
category), across 7,557 candidates. Meta received R\$ 288 million of this
directly; dLocal and Ebanx received another R\$ 114 million.

Adding the intermediaries, Meta would have received **up to R\$ 404 million,
8.7% of all contracted spending and about 97% of boosting**. The upper bound
assumes that everything paid to the intermediaries went to Meta. This is
plausible: no description of these payments names another platform, Google
stopped selling political ads in Brazil in 2024 and TikTok does not accept
political ads. The data do not establish the final destination of each payment.

WhatsApp boosting, where it exists, is bought from Meta itself (ads that open a
chat) and is already counted. Kwai (Joyo Tecnologia) received R\$ 2 million.
:::

## Meta in the campaigns

```{=html}
<section class="fornecedores-app" data-view="meta" data-lang="en" data-base="data/" aria-label="Direct payments to Meta"></section>
```

Meta's weight varies by office: 5% of spending for governors and federal
deputies, 7% for president and state deputies, 9% for senators and 14% for
district deputies. By party, PL paid Meta the most (R\$ 64 million); PT and PL devote a similar share
of their spending, close to 7.5%. The table's percentage is the share of the
candidate's total spending that went to Meta.

## How to read

- **Individuals** (canvassers, street mobilisation, freelancers) total R\$ 1.40
  billion. They appear as a single bar, without names or tax IDs.
- **Party spending** on behalf of candidates is excluded: the data cover each
  candidate's own campaign account. Donations from one candidate to another count
  as the donor's expense.
- Suppliers are identified by CNPJ (company tax ID). The name shown is the Federal
  Revenue name when the TSE provides it.
- A large supplier may pass part of the value on to others. The data do not show
  that path.

## Data and reproduction

Source: Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, [Open Data Portal](https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/dataset/prestacao-de-contas-eleitorais-2026),
file `despesas_contratadas_candidatos_2026_BRASIL.csv` generated on 18/10/2026.
The script [`shared-pipeline/fornecedores/010_build_fornecedores_2026.R`](https://github.com/mancano-tales/open-data-analysis/blob/main/shared-pipeline/fornecedores/010_build_fornecedores_2026.R)
downloads the file and builds the aggregates used here:

- [Overall summary (JSON)](data/resumo.json)
- [Totals by candidate, including Meta (CSV)](data/candidatos.csv)
- [Candidates who paid Meta (CSV)](data/meta-candidatos.csv)
- [Suppliers by party (JSON)](data/partidos.json)
